frames.observation: Lead-in at14.816667 before selected takeoff interval; near-neutral sword.
First lowering; right glove starts leaving lower edge.
Takeoff inertia low point: guard/hand below frame; shield nearly leaves bottom.
Rebound starts while sword leans farther left; wrist still below crop.
Airborne rebound raises both equipment pieces; glove visible but wrist joint not reliably localizable.
Wrist joint partly cropped lower-right; more connected right forearm/glove visible at high pose.
High pose continues; shield rim reaches highest observed sampled position.
Second rapid dip/landing response: full blade tip comes into frame; hand drops below.
Sword foreshortened with visible tip and left lean; not enlarged/tilted up-right. Shield begins rebound.
Damped recovery; blade rises beyond top again.
Returns toward ordinary locomotion framing at16.333333.
One-source-frame follow-through after the selected jump range; no isolated clip cut.

direction: Boundary includes f889=14.816667s lead-in, f890=14.833333s first selected lowering, through f980=16.333333s recovery plus f981=16.350000s continuity check. The video shows continuous motion; these are not hard animation cuts.
Observed pose order: both equipment pieces sink (15.000000), rebound high (15.500000–15.666667), dip/foreshorten again (15.833333–16.000000), then settle (16.166667–16.350000).
Shield top rim moves y≈0.817 at14.833333→0.928 at15.000000→0.647 at15.666667. Left-arm movement is a major visual cue; a shield remaining at y≈0.65 during takeoff would miss it.
At15.000000 the sword guard and wrist are below frame. At15.500000–15.666667 the glove and some connected wrist appear lower-right. None of these poses show a detached shoulder entering from above.

At16.000000 the sword tip is visible at(0.699,0.163), guard≈(0.763,0.942), blade leans left. The visible full blade and reduced projected length are essential to the landing response; expanding it toward upper-right produces the wrong silhouette.

Takeoff/air/landing names describe visible inertia interpretation. Exact foot-ground contact time, trajectory height, gravity and3D pose cannot be measured from these first-person frames; game landing should remain grounded in actual collision.
